App.Title: EMMA - installation
App.LoadFailed: EMMA could not read the installation.

Root.Heading: Foundry VTT {version}
Root.UnusedNote: Worlds without a record may run some of them.
Root.PendingNote: Of those, {count} only when next run: modules the worlds run now require them, updated since the worlds last ran.
Root.UnrecordedNote: A world without a record has not been opened with EMMA 0.9 or later active. Open it once, with EMMA active, and EMMA records its setup. Until then EMMA cannot tell which modules it runs.
Root.Guard: Let Foundry install and update packages here
Root.GuardHint: While this is off, Foundry's Install, Update and Update All buttons on this screen are disabled, so that packages do not change behind EMMA's back.

World.CoreChange: Foundry VTT: last ran with {recorded}, {installed} installed
World.Unrecorded: This world has no record: it has not been opened with EMMA 0.9 or later active. Open it once, with EMMA active, and EMMA records its setup.
World.Need: {title}: now required by {modules}, updated since the world last ran
World.Unreadable: EMMA cannot read this world's record. Open the world once, with EMMA active, to record its setup again.

ModuleInfo.ActiveInNone: Not active in any recorded world.
ModuleInfo.NeededNext: Will need it when next run: it is now required by {modules}, updated since the world last ran.

Refused: EMMA manages packages on this screen. To let Foundry install and update them, open EMMA from the menu and say so there.

System.NoWorlds: No world uses this game system.

Update.Unresolved: EMMA found no working setup for {count} recorded worlds, so nothing they use is offered an update.
Update.Hidden: Updates in the rows under it
Update.HiddenBlocked: Newer versions EMMA cannot offer in the rows under it
Update.BlockedWhy: EMMA cannot make every world that uses it consistent with this update.
Update.HeldUnrecorded: {world} has no EMMA record, so EMMA cannot tell whether the modules it runs would work with it.
Update.HeldUnresolved: EMMA found no working setup for {world}, so nothing it uses is updated.
Update.HeldInconsistent: In {world}, the other packages it runs cannot all work with it.
Update.NeedsCore: It needs Foundry VTT {core} or later, which is not installed.
Update.Checking: Checking which versions work with what is chosen…
Update.NoneFit: No other version works with what is chosen.
Update.NoManifestExplained: EMMA identified this version, but could not locate a manifest URL for it alone, so it cannot install it. A package's own manifest URL usually gives only its newest version. This version cannot be chosen.
Update.TakeOut: The plan cannot take it as it is: to choose it, take {choices} out of the plan.
Update.NoVerdict: EMMA has no verdict on this version, as nothing says which Foundry VTT builds it works with.
Update.CoreFits: Every package the recorded worlds run works with it.
Update.JudgedIn: As in {world}, the world that uses it where it fits least.
Update.Unlisted: Not on Foundry's package listing: its author has published it elsewhere, such as on GitLab, ahead of the listing, so Foundry's installer does not offer it.
Update.NeedsModule: Finding updates needs the EMMA module installed.
Update.ModuleTooOld: Finding updates needs a newer EMMA module than {version}.
Update.ExtensionTooOld: EMMA module {version} needs a newer browser extension to find updates.

Plan.NewestNeeds: The plan can take it only without {choices}.
Plan.NewestUnavailable: The plan cannot take it, whatever is taken out of it.
Plan.BackupUses: It uses {packages}, which the plan changes.
Plan.Recommended: Recommended, as the plan changes Foundry VTT
Plan.SnapshotNote: EMMA: before the update plan of {date}
Plan.NotEnough: Not enough space: needs about {required}, {available} free

Uninstall.Heading: Uninstall
Uninstall.NoUndo: Uninstalling deletes it from the server, with any data it keeps there, and cannot be undone. A snapshot keeps a copy.
Uninstall.Refused: EMMA cannot uninstall {title}, as it would break what uses it:
Uninstall.WorldSystem: {world} uses it as its game system.
Uninstall.WorldNeeds: {world} will need it when next run.
Uninstall.Warnings: EMMA cannot tell whether uninstalling it breaks these:
Uninstall.Unrecorded: {world} has no record, so it may run it.
Uninstall.Orphaned: {module} is left with no game system it runs in.

Run.Confirm: Run the plan? EMMA will, in order:
Run.StepSnapshot: make a snapshot of the installation
Run.StepCore: stop before updating Foundry VTT to {version}: the steps after it wait for another run
Run.Ran: The plan ran: every step is done.
Run.BeforeCore: The plan stopped before updating Foundry VTT to {version}.
Run.NoSnapshots: Foundry offers no way to make a snapshot here.
Run.NoBackups: Foundry offers no way to back a world up here.
Run.NoInstalls: Foundry offers no way to install packages here.
Run.NoManifest: EMMA has no manifest URL for {title} {version} alone, so cannot install it.

Core.Heading: Updating Foundry VTT to {version}
Core.Warning: Updating Foundry VTT in place is not recommended. It replaces the software every world on this server runs on, and there is no undoing it from here: if the new build, or a package on it, misbehaves, worlds may not open until Foundry VTT is put back by hand and the snapshot restored.
Core.Test: Test an update on a separate copy of Foundry VTT first, with a copy of your data, as Foundry's guide shows:
Core.NoUpdateMode: This Foundry VTT was started with in-place updates switched off (--noupdate), so it cannot be updated from here. Update it the way it was installed: for example a new image for a container, your host's control panel, or a fresh install of the build.
Core.Checking: Asking Foundry which build its updater would install…
Core.CheckFailed: Foundry could not say which build its updater would install, so it cannot be updated from here.
Core.NoTarget: Foundry's updater offers no build to update to: {message}
Core.OtherTarget: Foundry's updater would install {target}, not {version}: it installs only the newest build on its channel ({channel}). Choose {target} in the plan, or install {version} by other means.
Core.Manual: Foundry installs {version} only by hand, as a new install, so it cannot be updated from here.
Core.Confirm: If you are sure, Foundry's own updater will download {version}, install it over this one, and stop or restart the server. EMMA keeps the rest of the plan, to restore once Foundry VTT is on {version}.
Core.Update: Update Foundry VTT to {version} in place
Core.Begun: Foundry VTT is updating to {version}. The server stops or restarts once it is done; open this page again then.
Core.Kept: EMMA kept the rest of the plan, and restores it once Foundry VTT is on that build.
Core.NotKept: EMMA could not keep the rest of the plan, as the browser refused to store it: plan it again then.
Core.Resumed: The plan from before Foundry VTT's update to {version} is back: run it to finish.

Group.ModulesNote: {count} modules installed, by the game systems they are for. A module for several systems is in each of them.
Group.UniversalNote: Modules that name no game system, for use with any.
Group.SystemNote: Modules that name {title} among the game systems they are for.
Group.SystemMissingNote: Modules that name {title} among the game systems they are for. {title} is not installed.
